headline: Kai, unless ninety-three percent of the market is wrong, the Fed raises rates this afternoon for the first time since July 2023.
subline: The quarter-point move to 3.75–4.00 percent lands at 2 p.m. ET, August retail sales hit at 8:30, and oil holds above $100 with the ten-year parked at five.
asof: Pre-market · as of 6:50 AM ET · index strip shows Tuesday's close, futures flat-to-higher pre-dawn · every figure links to its source below

items.title: A quarter-point hike, 93 percent priced, lands today
items.sentence: Markets put roughly 93 percent odds on a quarter-point rise to a 3.75–4.00 percent range at 2 p.m. ET — the first increase since July 2023 — with new chair Kevin Warsh's own posture the day's remaining question mark, per Kiplinger's live blog.

items.title: Ten-year pauses near five after five-session climb
items.sentence: The 10-year yield eased to 4.99 percent this morning after five straight rising sessions carried it to levels last seen in July 2007, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Rates squeezed the hyperscalers into Tuesday's close
items.sentence: The S&P 500 fell 0.45 percent Tuesday to 7,600.12 — the Dow lost 0.63 percent and the Nasdaq 100 0.65 percent — with credit-sensitive AI names hit hardest as borrowing costs rose, Oracle down 3.1 percent and Amazon 2 percent, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Oil backs off on a surprise inventory build
items.sentence: Brent slipped 0.99 percent to $107.67 and WTI 1.75 percent to $103.97 after U.S. crude stockpiles rose 7.14 million barrels against expected draws — even with Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline still shut and Libya idling two oilfields, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Gold reclaims $4,300 ahead of the decision
items.sentence: Gold rose 1.11 percent to $4,340.11 as momentum in oil and bond yields faded ahead of the Fed and other central-bank decisions this week, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Clarity Act dies 49–50; bitcoin holds the mid-$75,000s
items.sentence: The Senate's crypto market-structure bill fell 49–50 on Tuesday's cloture vote, short of even a simple majority, triggering roughly $570 million in long liquidations, per CoinDesk. Bitcoin, which traded near $80,000 before the vote, sits at $75,844 this morning — down 2.2 percent over 24 hours, per CoinDesk's price tracker.

items.title: House votes to end the Iran war
items.sentence: Seven Republicans joined Democrats as the House passed a resolution directing an end to U.S. hostilities with Iran, a bipartisan rebuke as casualties mount, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Iran's top diplomat heads to Beijing
items.sentence: Tehran is testing diplomatic paths as its foreign minister travels to China, raising the question of whether Beijing can broker an end to the war, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: NATO jet downs Russian drone over Lithuania
items.sentence: A NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania as the EU chief warned border incursions risk a wider conflict, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: US plans $2.8bn bomb sale to Israel
items.sentence: The Trump administration plans a $2.8 billion sale of 2,000-pound bombs to Israel, signaling continued military support amid the regional war, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Gaza building collapse kills at least 16
items.sentence: A residential building collapsed in Gaza with six families reportedly trapped beneath the rubble, killing at least 16 as rescue crews dig for survivors, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Three rival labs coordinate on AI safety
items.sentence: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind have spent weeks discussing shared safety measures — embedding third-party evaluators and possibly an industry standards body — even as some flag antitrust risk in the coordination, per TechCrunch.

items.title: SK Hynix talks with Intel lift both stocks
items.sentence: SK Hynix is reportedly in talks with Intel about manufacturing memory chips in the U.S. for the first time, sending Intel up more than 3 percent pre-market, per Stocktwits.

items.title: Nvidia's Rubin doubles Blackwell in early testing
items.sentence: SemiAnalysis pre-release testing has the Rubin NVL72 delivering 2.1 times Blackwell's throughput at 100 tokens per second, per AI Weekly's daily brief.

items.title: AI agents breach 395 organizations in 48 hours
items.sentence: AI agents exploited two PaperCut flaws to compromise 395 organizations across 48 countries within 48 hours — 11 breaches came in 26 seconds — per AI Weekly's daily brief.

items.title: Starship Flight 14 targets first orbit September 22
items.sentence: SpaceX is targeting September 22 for Starship's fourteenth flight, its first attempt to reach orbit, pending regulatory approval, per Stocktwits.
